meta.title: Xcasca Color Scheme Gallery: Terminal Themes to Preview and Download
meta.description: Preview and download free terminal color schemes for Xcasca, including Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox, Catppuccin and Tokyo Night, for desktop and mobile.
meta.ogDescription: Preview and download free terminal color schemes for Xcasca, including Dracula, Nord, Gruvbox, Catppuccin and Tokyo Night.
theme.label: Theme
intro.title: Color schemes for the Xcasca terminal
intro.body: Pick a scheme to see it on a real-looking terminal session, then download the file and import it in Xcasca 1.1.2 or later, on the desktop or on your phone. Every file here was exported from the app itself, so it imports as it is.
fineprint: An unofficial project, unrelated to the company behind Xcasca.
gallery.label: Color schemes
search.label: Search color schemes
export.label: For other apps
export.note: The same colors in another terminal app’s format. The selection becomes a solid color, and the search highlight colors, which only Xcasca has, are left out.
terminal.label: A terminal drawn with the selected color scheme. Click it to type.
palette.label: Colors
viewer.hint: Click the terminal to type in it, and try ls or pwd. Click a color to copy its hex value. The highlighted text shows the selection color.
apply.title: Apply a downloaded scheme
apply.body: Import the .xccolorscheme file once, then pick it for any session. The scheme is stored like the ones you make yourself, and syncs with your other devices if you use sync.
steps.desktop.1: Open the ⋮ menu at the top right, then Tools > Terminal Color Schemes...
steps.desktop.1.alt: The menu open on Tools, with Terminal Color Schemes highlighted
steps.desktop.2: Click ⋮ under the list, choose Import..., and pick the file you downloaded.
steps.desktop.2.alt: The Terminal Color Schemes window with Import highlighted in its menu
steps.desktop.3: The scheme joins the list. Click Close.
steps.desktop.3.alt: The imported scheme selected in the list, with its colors shown
steps.desktop.4: Click the session properties button on the toolbar, then Current Session. Default Session sets it for new sessions instead.
steps.desktop.4.alt: The session properties button with Current Session highlighted
steps.desktop.5: Under Appearance, choose the scheme in Color Scheme and click OK.
steps.desktop.5.alt: Session properties with the color scheme chosen and OK highlighted
steps.desktop.6: The terminal takes the new colors right away.
steps.desktop.6.alt: The terminal drawn with the new color scheme
steps.android.1: On the home screen, open the menu at the bottom left and tap Terminal Color Schemes.
steps.android.1.alt: The app menu with Terminal Color Schemes highlighted
steps.android.2: Tap +, then Import, and pick the downloaded file.
steps.android.2.alt: The add menu with Import highlighted
steps.android.3.alt: The imported scheme highlighted in the list
steps.android.4: In Sessions, press and hold a session, then tap Edit.
steps.android.4.alt: A session's menu with Edit highlighted
steps.android.5: Under Appearance, pick the scheme in Color Scheme, then tap the check mark to save.
steps.android.5.alt: Session properties with the color scheme chosen and the save button highlighted
steps.android.6: Open the session to see the new colors.
steps.android.6.alt: The terminal drawn with the new color scheme

editor.meta.title: Xcasca Color Scheme Editor: Make a Terminal Theme
editor.meta.description: Make your own terminal color scheme for Xcasca on a live preview, starting from Dracula, Nord or any other scheme, and download it as a .xccolorscheme file.
editor.title: Make your own color scheme
editor.body: Start from a scheme in the gallery or from a file you have, change any color, and watch the terminal follow. When you like it, download the file and import it in Xcasca like any other scheme.
editor.name: Name
editor.hint: Your work is kept in this browser until you start over. Made something worth sharing? Add it to the gallery.

runtime.editor.nameTaken: The gallery has a scheme with this name; the app numbers a copy, such as "Name (1)".
runtime.editor.nameGallery: Fine for the app. For the gallery, use up to 64 letters, digits and spaces in English.
runtime.editor.importError: This file is not a color scheme Xcasca can import.
